parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, and documented protections include a workplace gender-identity discrimination ban and a media hate-speech ban, though hate-crime aggravation excludes gender identity and the 2025-26 roadmap measures are unconfirmed. Attitudes are mixed: general acceptance polling is rising, but taboo framing and ex-gay messaging persist. The main visitor-facing exposure is border stops of male-marker holders under martial law, documented by a national NGO and not shown to have ended. This is a document-mismatch exposure that reaches any visitor with a male marker. Diagnosis barriers and the open mobilisation-exemption question mainly affect residents. Violence evidence is dated (2011-2013) with no trans-specific rate, so that axis is weakly assessed, and the police response record is poor. Net: Elevated Risk, with the border exposure as the main drag on an otherwise partly protected jurisdiction.
